summary: Cast-iron tower of 1885 at the end of the Lewes breakwater; Delaware Breakwater Range front light 1903-1918; automated 1950; state-owned; accompanied visits only.

lens.where: original fourth-order lens; USLHS lists a 375 mm current optic

structures.material: four tiers of cast-iron plates lined with two feet of brick
structures.note: 22 ft diameter at base on a circular concrete foundation (marker). Height disputed: 49 ft (NRHP) vs 56 ft base to lantern center (USLHS).
100 ft west of the tower; held fuel for the light until electrification (NRHP)

access.note: State of Delaware: access prohibited except accompanied visits conducted by Cape Water Tours; viewable from Cape Henlopen State Park. The USLHS record says open to public.

events.note: Cast-iron tower built at the east end of the inner breakwater

notes_for_editor: Checked this round. Marker SC-185 page read: brown conical tower, cast-iron plates, 22 ft base, fourth-order lens, 61 ft focal plane, fog trumpet November 1885, range front 1903-1918, automated 11 July 1950, Pilots' Association in the 1960s and 1970s, decommissioned 1996, conveyed 5 February 1999, installed 2004. NRHP 89000289 read: 49 ft tower; 1912 oil shed 100 ft west; 1926 light on the east end of the Harbor of Refuge breakwater, replacing one damaged in 1920; 1833 Army request and west-end placement; a 1848 light placed on the northeast end in the description and on the western end in the history (the story reports both, and the two passages are not reconciled). USLHS place record read: location 'LEWES HARBOR/DELAWARE BAY ENTRANCE', tower 56 ft to lantern centre, 'Open to Public: Yes'; its principal-keeper and assistant lists match the JSON roster line for line (10 principal, 19 first assistant, 10 second assistant). State historic-sites page read: access prohibited except accompanied visits by Cape Water Tours; viewable from Cape Henlopen State Park. Friends page read: 1885 build, first lit October 1885, range front May 1903, keepers on board through 1950. Light-House Board volume annualreportlig01statgoog: FY1893 heading (line 73) and FY1894 heading (about line 15790) bound the two reports; the 673-hour entry (No. 368, scan p. 110) is in the FY1893 report; the 'Daboll trampet' passage (scan p. 406) is in the FY1894 report. FY1899 heading read in annualreportlig04statgoog; the entry says 'some 607 hours' and the story now says 'about 607 hours'. OCR CAUTION (for the checker): the fog trumpet's maker is printed 'Baboll' in the 1893 OCR (the 1899 OCR reads 'Daboll'); the 1893 and 1899 printed page numbers were not confirmed. OCR CAUTION (1915 table): Commissioner's 1915 'Saving of Life and Property' table, scan p. 65, is OCR'd in columns: the names column reads 'H. C. Wingate, keeper, and H. P. Marshall, first assistant keeper, Delaware Breakwater Range Front Light Station, Del.' and the 'Nature of assistance' column is separated and garbled. The Wingate/Marshall pairing with the assistance is not legible, so the story says only that the list names them and that the account does not say what they did. The page image (scan p. 65) was NOT viewed: no page image is cached and it was not fetched; the checker should view scan p. 65 before publication. Printed page is 60 (OCR page head). CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN: tower height 49 ft (NRHP) vs 56 ft (USLHS, Friends); access 'open to public' (USLHS) vs state's accompanied-visit rule; the 1848 light's location within the NRHP (northeast end vs western end); Friends page last updated 2018, so the current access statement is taken from the state page. NOT USED: a 1973 airport-beacon change in a search snippet of the USLHS record (not in the cached page); the NRHP freighter passage (ambiguous as to which lighthouse); Cape Water Tours' own pages (the state page names them). No wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the sources read; the 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter holds the fog-signal record only. Newspaper search for Willard H. Hall returned unrelated pages in an earlier pass; not repeated.
